title: When Imperfect Automated Fact-Checking Backfires: Social Learning in the Presence of Misinformation
abstract: arXiv:2611.08053v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Automated fact-checking tools, cheap and fast but imperfect, are increasingly available on social platforms. We study when such tools can backfire in a sequential social learning model of misinformation. Agents observe an article's reliability and their predecessors' actions, which indicate whether they liked or disliked the article. They may also pay to fact-check it. We examine how welfare, defined as the probability of a correct cascade, changes when a free, error-prone automated tool supplements costly but perfectly accurate manual fact-checking. Two opposing effects arise. Broader use of fact-checking helps agents escape wrong cascades. At the same time, errors from the automated tool can mislead agents who would otherwise have verified the article perfectly, reducing the likelihood of correct cascades. translated_title: 当不完美的事实核查适得其反时：错误信息存在下的社会学习
translated_abstract: 自动事实核查工具成本低廉、速度快但并不完美，如今在社交平台上日益普及。我们在一个关于错误信息的序贯社会学习模型中研究此类工具何时可能适得其反。智能体会观察一篇文章的可靠性以及前序者的行为（即他们表示喜欢或不喜欢该文章），他们也可能付费对该文章进行事实核查。我们考察当免费但易出错的自动化工具作为昂贵却完全准确的人工事实核查的补充时，社会福利（定义为形成正确信息级联的概率）会如何变化。研究发现了两种相反的效应：更广泛地使用事实核查能帮助智能体摆脱错误的级联；与此同时，自动工具产生的错误可能误导那些原本会进行完美人工核查的智能体，从而降低形成正确级联的可能性。我们证明，当真实文章的信息量不太大时，引入该工具会严格降低中等可靠性文章的社会福利……
tldr: 该研究通过序贯社会学习模型证明，免费但易错的自动事实核查工具是一把双刃剑——它虽能帮助用户摆脱错误的舆论级联，但其错误可能误导原本会进行完美人工核查的用户，从而反而降低中等可靠性文章下的社会福利。
en_tdlr: This paper shows via a sequential social learning model that free but imperfect automated fact-checking is a double-edged sword: it can help agents escape wrong information cascades, yet its errors may mislead agents who would otherwise have verified perfectly, strictly lowering welfare for articles of intermediate reliability.
